body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Tuesday, August 18, 2026 — a day that’s starting off warm, with temperatures already hitting 90° at Meadows Field. We’re keeping an eye on a moderate air quality reading of 61 and no active weather alerts. Our top story this morning is the arrest of a California City man after hundreds of pounds of narcotics and a firearm were seized. Overnight, Kern County saw its share of incidents, from a truck fire that spread into hillside vegetation to a barrage of shots fired in the south end. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, the news, and what’s coming up this week.

## The Kern Overnight

The night began with a significant fire response west of Bakersfield when a truck fire that reportedly tipped over and burned down a trailer pushed into the hillside. The incident escalated into a wildland response around 9:47 p.m., drawing multiple engines, a dozer, helicopter 409, and a water tender among the ordered resources. Crews worked to access the burn as the reporting party pointed out lights on the hill. A few hours later, just before 3:45 a.m., a 53-foot trailer north of Pond on Garzoli Road was fully involved, with a spot of grass fire spreading alongside it. Battalion crews responded to what dispatch dubbed the Garzoli Incident and remained on scene for hotspots. Meanwhile, in the south end, a caller reported roughly 30 shots fired, mostly in a field near Panama Lane and South Allen Road just before 10:45 p.m. The call stood for service while units investigated. Elsewhere, a welfare check near the Wells Fargo on Columbus Street escalated around 3:06 a.m. when a man on a bicycle was approached by subjects, an impact sound was heard, and a fight involving three people ensued. Two suspects fled northbound Columbus, and units searched the area. In Delano, a big-rig incident with a load of table grapes brought a roadway closure just after 4 a.m., with Environmental Health notified. The rest of the night was the usual spread of domestic calls, ShotSpotter activations, welfare checks, and small fires.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather is shaping up to be a warm one, with a high near 98° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 90° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and we’re tracking a moderate air quality reading of 61. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County at this time. Expect plenty of sunshine throughout the day, with clear skies overnight. If you’re planning outdoor activities, be sure to stay hydrated and take breaks in the shade during the warmest parts of the afternoon.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that a California City man was arrested after hundreds of pounds of narcotics and a firearm were seized.** The Kern County Sheriff’s Office said the arrest came after a search warrant was served, uncovering a significant stash of drugs and a weapon. This operation is part of ongoing efforts to combat drug trafficking in the region, and the investigation is still active. **KGET 17 also told us that a Bakersfield man died after being stabbed by a woman on White Lane.** The incident is under investigation, and details are still emerging about what led to the altercation. **According to 23ABC, California is holding firm on school vaccine rules as national rates dip.** New CDC data shows that kindergarten vaccination rates are slipping across the country, raising questions about how many children are starting school without all of their required shots. In California, the law requires children entering TK through 12th grade to have documentation of required vaccinations, and unlike many states, California does not allow religious or personal-belief exemptions. Kern Public Health says virtual schools may be exempt from immunization requirements, and when looking at classroom-based schools, the rate rises to 93.7%, similar to the state average. **23ABC also said that the fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield continues.** Buck Owens' Crystal Palace closed about a year ago, and its future remains uncertain. One offer on the table would mean tearing it down, but the Buck Owens Private Foundation hopes to find a buyer who will reopen and reimagine the venue in a manner that brings the building back to life. The foundation has received several offers, including one that would be a tear-down, but the hope is that the right person will step forward with a plan to keep the spirit of the Bakersfield Sound alive.

## Something good

The community of Bakersfield and Kern County will have the opportunity to participate in City Council elections during the November 2026 General Election. This upcoming event will allow residents to exercise their civic duty and contribute to shaping local governance. Depending on which city a Kern County resident lives in, their council can be structured in a few different ways: districts, at-large, or a mix of both. District elections require candidates to live within the district they represent, and voters only get to vote for candidates in the district they reside in. At-large elections only require candidates to live within city limits, voters generally vote for several candidates on one ballot, and the top vote-getters are awarded a seat on the council. However, similar to the 2024 election, some residents in Wasco and Tehachapi likely won't vote for their city council members as they are running unopposed. Wasco City Council is slated to vote on cancelling the District 3 race where Valentin Medina is the only candidate. A spokesperson for the City of Tehachapi indicated the city intends to do the same, as there is only one candidate per race on their city council ballot. However, McFarland is unable to take advantage of the same scenario despite only having one candidate per district. City Clerk Erika De La Cruz told 23ABC in an email, "In this case, two measures and one initiative have qualified for the upcoming election. As a result, the City cannot proceed under Section 10229(a). Additionally, the Kern County Elections Office has confirmed that there is no provision in the Elections Code that would allow the City to cancel an election when there are other items on the ballot." This is a great opportunity for residents to get involved and make their voices heard in local government.

## Coming up this week

There are several public meetings and events worth noting this week. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee will meet at 12:00 p.m., and the Historic Preservation Commission will convene at 4:00 p.m. Also on Tuesday, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission will meet at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board will meet at 10:00 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission will meet at 5:30 p.m. In addition to these meetings, there are several events at the Fox Theater. On Saturday, August 22, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform. On Monday, August 24, the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 will be available. On Thursday, August 27, Rodney Carrington will take the stage. On Friday, August 28, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE will be held. And on Saturday, August 29, Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will perform. Be sure to check the Fox Theater’s website for tickets and more information.
